member.name: T:KeshavSingh.Core.Models.LoginAudit
member.summary:
Security audit event. Never stores passwords, tokens, or other personal data. Backs . Event names come from — apps should not define their own duplicate event-name constants.
Authentication is not the only thing worth auditing: an app may also record its own administrative actions (a role granted, a setting changed) into the same collection, so that "who did what" is one timeline rather than two. and exist for those — an auth event leaves both null.
because this collection is shared: an app writing a richer document must not break the retention sweep or the analytics reads, which deserialize every row through this type.

member.name: P:KeshavSingh.Core.Models.LoginAudit.Target
member.summary: What the event acted ON, when that differs from the actor — the edited user's email, the settings section, the collection a console write touched. Null for authentication events, where the actor and the subject are the same account.

member.name: P:KeshavSingh.Core.Models.LoginAudit.Details
member.summary:
A short, human-readable summary of the change, for the audit viewer.
MUST NOT contain personal data, secrets, query filters or document bodies: this is read back by anyone with the audit permission, and it is the same reason the DB console logs operation-and-collection rather than what was queried. Say "3 roles granted", not which records matched.

Backs the auth engine's with a Mongo collection ("refresh_tokens"). Shared so every app doesn't hand-roll the same adapter.
Single-session-per-user enforcement is decided and orchestrated entirely by AuthEngine now (scoped per , with an explicit block-and-confirm step) — this store is a plain, policy-free CRUD adapter.

member.name: T:KeshavSingh.Core.Roles
member.summary: The fixed set of roles shared by every app in the keshavsingh.in family. Access is default-deny: a user can do nothing unless a role explicitly grants it (enforced by [Authorize(Roles = ...)]). Kept in one place because the identity provider (admin.keshavsingh.in) issues these role names into the JWT, and every resource server (e.g. the blog) authorizes against the SAME names — if they drifted, cross-app authorization would silently break.

member.name: T:KeshavSingh.Core.SsoCorsExtensions
member.summary:
Registers the cross-subdomain SSO CORS policy shared by every app in the keshavsingh.in family.
This policy is credentialed, and the same browsers that satisfy it also hold the .keshavsingh.in SSO cookie — so whatever it admits is, in practice, a fully trusted origin. Two consequences shape the API below:
Prefer an explicit allowlist. The wildcard-subdomain predicate trusts every current AND future *.keshavsingh.in host, which means a subdomain whose DNS record outlives the service behind it (a retired GitHub Pages or Render CNAME) can be claimed by someone else and inherit that trust. Pass the origins you actually run to
whenever you know them.
localhost is development-only. It used to be allowed unconditionally, which left http://localhost:* as an accepted credentialed origin in production for no functional gain — local development runs the API on localhost too, which is same-origin.

member.name: M:KeshavSingh.Core.SsoCorsExtensions.AddKeshavSsoCors(Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.IServiceCollection,System.String,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyCollection{System.String},System.Boolean,System.String)
member.param: The exact origins to trust. When non-empty this is the whole allowlist and the wildcard-subdomain rule is not used at all — the safer configuration, and the one to use in production. When null/empty the policy falls back to "any subdomain of over https".
Whether to additionally trust localhost on any port/scheme. Pass env.IsDevelopment(); never true in production.
Root domain for the wildcard fallback.

member.summary: Decides whether one origin is trusted. Exposed so an app can unit-test its own allowlist, and so the rule lives in exactly one place.

member.name: T:KeshavSingh.Core.WhatsAppNotifier
member.summary: Sends operational/security alerts (e.g. account lockouts) to a single admin phone number via the Meta WhatsApp Cloud API. Shared so every app doesn't hand-roll the same HTTP call. No-ops (logging instead) when disabled or unconfigured, so it's always safe to call.
member.remarks: Freeform text only delivers within the 24h "customer service window" opened by the recipient messaging the business number first; outside that window Meta requires a pre-approved message template instead. For a fixed alert-to number, send that first WhatsApp message manually once to open the window (or set up a template) before relying on this for time-sensitive alerts.

member.name: M:KeshavSingh.Core.WhatsAppNotifier.SendMessageToAsync(System.String,System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Sends a freeform WhatsApp message to an arbitrary number (e.g. a 2FA OTP to the signed-in user's own phone), reusing the same access token/phone number ID. No-ops when unconfigured.
